x: Andhra (State), formed on 1 October 1953 and renamed Andhra Pradesh in 1956, was the first state formed on a linguistic basis after independence. Orissa (1936) was a pre-independence linguistic province; Maharashtra came in 1960.

s: From which state was Andhra Pradesh carved out as a state in 1953?
x: Andhra State (1953) was carved out of the Telugu-speaking districts of Madras State; Telangana joined from Hyderabad State only in 1956.

s: Which of the following was the first state of independent India formed on the basis of language?
x: Andhra (State), formed on 1 October 1953 from Madras State, was the first state of independent India formed on the basis of language; it became Andhra Pradesh in 1956. Kerala and Tamil Nadu came later.

src: APPSC 2019 Various non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
s: What was the capital of the 'Andhra State" which was created in 1953?
x: Kurnool was the capital of Andhra State (1953); Hyderabad became capital only of Andhra Pradesh in 1956.

s: In post independent India, in 1953, Andhra State was the first state to be formed on linguistic basis. Which of the following was the capital of this Andhra State?
x: Andhra State's capital was Kurnool, chosen over Vijayawada by an Assembly vote of 80 to 79. Hyderabad became capital only after 1956, and Amaravati is the capital of the residuary state after 2014.

src: APPSC Various Non-Gazetted Posts (Limited Recruitment) - Sam
s: Before 1956, which city was the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Kurnool was the capital of Andhra State (formed 1 October 1953) until 1956; Hyderabad became the capital of Andhra Pradesh from 1 November 1956.

s: Which is the first ever state constituted on linguistic basis?
x: Andhra State (1953), the forerunner of Andhra Pradesh, was the first state of independent India constituted on a linguistic basis. Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka (Mysore) were reorganised only in 1956.

src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer in A.P. Tribal Welfar
s: Who among the following was not a member of the State Reorganisation Commission of 1953?
x: The SRC had Fazl Ali (Chairman), H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar; Tej Bahadur Sapru was never a member.

s: On which date in 1953 did the Government of India appoint the States Reorganisation Commission?
x: On 22 December 1953 the Prime Minister announced in Parliament that the States Reorganisation Commission would be appointed (Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar, H.N. Kunzru); the formal resolution followed on 29 December 1953.

src: APPSC 2019 Various non Gazetted Posts Limited Recruitment
s: Who headed the States Reorganisation Commission that was set up by the Government of India in December 1953?
x: Syed Fazl Ali, then Governor of Odisha, chaired the States Reorganisation Commission. C.M. Trivedi was AP's first Governor; Brahmananda Reddy and Sanjivaiah were later AP Chief Ministers.

s: Who was the President of the States Reorganization Commission?
x: The States Reorganisation Commission (December 1953) was chaired by Fazl Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members; Patel was not on it (he was on the JVP Committee).

s: In which year did Nehru appoint the State Reorganisation Committee (SRC)?
x: The SRC under Fazl Ali was appointed in December 1953 (announced 22 Dec, resolution 29 Dec) and reported on 30 September 1955.

s: On which date in 1953 did the Government of India appoint the States Reorganisation Commission?
x: On 22 December 1953 Nehru announced in Parliament that the States Reorganisation Commission would be appointed; the formal Home Ministry resolution was dated 29 December 1953.

s: Who is the chairman of states re-organization commission?
x: The SRC was chaired by Fazl Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members; Patel, Pattabhi Sitaramayya and Nehru formed the earlier JVP Committee.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: States Reorganization Commission was set up in 1953 under the Chairmanship of ..........
x: The States Reorganisation Commission set up in 1953 was chaired by Saiyid Fazl Ali, with H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar as members.

s: The Telugu-speaking State of Andhra Pradesh was formed in ____ on a linguistic basis, following the recommendations of the States' Reorganisation Commission
x: Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 under the States Reorganisation Act, after the SRC's report (1955). The printed key 1953 is the date of Andhra State, which came before the SRC was even appointed.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
s:
Which of the following statements are correct?

A. The State Reorganisation Act was enacted on 31 August 1956.

B. United Andhra Pradesh was established on 1 November 1956.

C. The report of the State Reorganisation Commission consists of four parts.
x: All three are correct: the SR Act (Act 37 of 1956) was enacted on 31 August 1956; united Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956; and the SRC report has four parts (Conditions of the Problem; Factors Bearing on Reorganisation; Proposals; Administrative and Allied Matters).

s: When was Andhra Pradesh formed as a linguistic state?
x:
Some keys: 1953 (Andhra State, the first linguistic state). Strictly: Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 (SR Act 1956; NextGen AP History Part 20 p.7).
Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956 by merging Andhra State with Telangana under the SR Act. If the setter meant Andhra State, the first linguistic state, the answer would be 1953. 1950 and 1960 are wrong in either reading.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: When was State Reorganization Act passed?
x: The States Reorganisation Act (Act 37 of 1956) was enacted on 31 August 1956 and took effect on 1 November 1956.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant in Dr. NTR University of Health Scien
s:
Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct regarding the recommendations of the States Reorganisation Commission (Fazal Ali Commission)?

A. Most of the Telugu regions wanted the division of Hyderabad State.

B. Kannada areas should be merged with Mysuru, and Marathwada areas should be merged with Bombay State.

C. If Kurnool is made the capital city, the problem of the permanent capital of Andhra Pradesh will also be solved.
x: A and B are correct: Hyderabad State was to be divided, with Kannada areas going to Mysore and Marathwada to Bombay. C is wrong: the SRC said the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad, not Kurnool, would solve Andhra's permanent-capital problem.

src: APPSC Assistant Tribal Welfare Officer (A.P. Tribal Welfare
s: Which of the following twin cities was recommended by the State Reorganisation Committee to be the capital of Andhra Pradesh?
x: Para 371 of the SRC report said 'the twin cities of Hyderabad and Secunderabad are very well suited to be the capital of Vishalandhra'. Telangana is a region, not a city.

src: Social and Cultural History of A.P and Welfare Programmes 20
s: Whose report submitted in 1955, pretty much conceded that India reorganized according to linguistic provinces?
x: The States Reorganisation Commission (Fazl Ali; Kunzru, Panikkar) reported in September 1955 and largely accepted linguistic states.

s: Which commission in its report (1948) opined that the creation of linguistic states posed a threat to national unity and integrity?
x: The S.K. Dhar (Linguistic Provinces) Commission's report of December 1948 held that linguistic states could hinder national unity and preferred administrative convenience. The JVP Report (1949) advised postponement; Wanchoo dealt with Andhra's separation (1953).

s: In 1948 which Commission, in its report opined that creation of linguistic states is a threat to unity and integrity of the country
x: The Dhar Commission (1948) saw the creation of linguistic states as a threat to national unity and preferred administrative convenience. The JVP Committee only advised postponement, and Wanchoo dealt with Andhra's separation.

s: With the formation of linguistic States
x: Supporters argued that a state run in the people's own language makes administration easier and closer to the people. 'Always strengthened/weakened' are absolute claims, and the 'administration becomes difficult' fear is not the accepted view.

s: Which Constitutional Amendment Act extended the jurisdiction of High Courts to Union Territories?
x: The Seventh Amendment Act, 1956 reorganised the states into 14 states and 6 UTs and extended the jurisdiction of High Courts to Union Territories; it also allowed a common High Court for two or more states.
